system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data engineer with 9 years of experience building and operating batch and streaming data platforms
across logistics, payments and retail. Owns production ingestion and orchestration, with a focus on
reusable tooling, tested transformations and reliable data contracts. Combines Python, SQL, Airflow
and dbt expertise with AWS cloud experience, dimensional modelling and hands-on platform
operations.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), SSIS
Warehouses and databases: Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server
Streaming and CDC: Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Snowpipe Streaming, AWS MSK
Cloud and engineering: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM), Docker, Git, GitHub Actions,
CI/CD, Terraform (basic)
Data quality and modelling: Great Expectations, JSON Schema, data contracts, dimensional
modelling, incremental models, pytest
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o.
03/2022 - present

PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party API data into Snowflake; participate in an on-call

• Designed and built a Kafka and Snowpipe Streaming pipeline processing approximately 30 million

replay tooling.
• Replaced hourly full-table PostgreSQL extracts with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica
CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
• Reduced monthly Snowflake costs from approximately 38,000 to 24,000 through warehouse sizing,
auto-suspend and removal of unused tables in 2024.
• Mentor two mid-level data engineers and run weekly data platform office hours.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay
09/2019 - 02/2022
• Built PySpark transaction reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR processing approximately 1.2 TB of
raw S3 files daily; reduced finance’s manual month-end reconciliation from approximately 3 days to
4 hours.
• Designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse with 30+ fact and dimension tables for finance and
risk; implemented Great Expectations checks on critical finance tables.
• Developed a reusable Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access adopted by four teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group
06/2017 - 08/2019

nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across 40+ stores.
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate | May 2024
OPEN SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package, fixing a pagination bug and
adding tests with Python and pytest (2023).
• Presented "Data contracts without the hype" at a regional data meetup (2024).
• Teach beginner SQL at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since
2021.
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Lena Varga-Holm
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer - Data Platform position. Your emphasis on
reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines closely matches my work: owning
production ingestion and orchestration, building shared Python tooling, and making data
quality part of delivery. I bring nine years of data engineering experience, including
transaction reconciliation and warehouse design in payments.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own an ingestion layer of approximately 140 Airflow DAGs and
participate in the platform’s on-call rotation. I migrated approximately 300 stored procedures
into dbt, introduced incremental models and slim CI, and helped bring nightly build time
from 5h10 to 1h35. Data contracts backed by JSON Schema and CI checks reduced
broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine to two per month. Alongside reliability, I
addressed operating costs: warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables
reduced the monthly Snowflake bill from approximately 38,000 to 24,000.
My payments experience would also be relevant to Halden Pay’s cross-border business
payments platform. At Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR
processing approximately 1.2 TB daily, reducing manual month-end reconciliation from
approximately three days to four hours. I designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse for
finance and risk and developed an S3 and Glue Data Catalog library used by four teams. My
cloud experience is in AWS, supported by the AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate
certification awarded in May 2024; Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Docker and GitHub Actions
provide substantial overlap with your engineering stack.
Your support for open-source contributions is particularly relevant to my two merged Airflow
provider pull requests, which fixed a pagination bug and added tests. I also mentor two
engineers and run weekly platform office hours, bringing practical experience of sharing
knowledge and supporting platform users. I would welcome a conversation about how I could
help Halden Pay build reusable platform capabilities and dependable data quality standards.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
